title: Earthquake interval · relative LOS coverage mosaic
notes: Each mosaic cell comes from one event group; the selected reference mode is recorded; dates and radar look vectors vary. Inspect the source-group and overlap-difference maps. This is not a common-date time series, east/west motion decomposition or a damage map.
The overlap difference includes viewing geometry, different post-event dates, reference choices and measurement errors; it is not an accuracy estimate.
All plotted regional comparisons use the same pixels valid on every selected date or pair. Per-date coverage is shown separately; missing coverage is never reported as zero change.
The shortest event-bracketing interval is selected. Any signal may also include other changes within that interval; this is not a building-damage map.

The main earthquake map is displacement in cm across the selected interval, not a rate. Positive is toward the satellite and negative away; neither is automatically east/west or up/down. Raw measured pairs in mm and interval rates remain in Advanced maps.
Each point is a separate pair interval, not a cumulative displacement time series or a fitted velocity.
Conversion is −λ × (phase − reference median)/(4π), in millimeters. Check product sign convention before assigning toward/away language.
Only the retained native connected component is used. Read the correction manifest: ionospheric subtraction is optional; tropospheric and tidal corrections are not assumed.
Reference stability is an assumption. No vertical motion, structural safety, failure probability or thaw depth is inferred.
Input is a local native-grid area extract, not a complete original NASA product; only the saved rectangle can be analyzed.
Only native connected component 1 retained before averaging. Labels are file-local; see the correction manifest for any explicitly applied screen.

report.headline: What these observations show
findings: 1 compatible GUNW observations cover 2026-06-18 to 2026-06-30. Regional comparisons use 50,173 common analysis cells (4049.561 km²).

Reference uses 979 identical cells across pairs. Pair network: 2 epochs, 1 connected component(s), 0 redundant edge(s). Read the P04 motion-model status or the other phase tools’ network-model status to see whether reconstruction was supported.
Selected event interval: 2026-06-18 to 2026-06-30. It strictly brackets the supplied date and is the shortest matching selected pair; other changes in that interval are not excluded.

Relative LOS displacement across this interval: spatial median -0.627 cm, p10 -20.885 cm and p90 3.366 cm. Positive is toward the satellite and negative away, relative to the saved reference; these spatial percentiles are not accuracy bounds.

event_mosaic.selection: Highest delivered accepted-sample coherence among valid event groups at each cell; ties use sorted group order. No overlap averaging or inferred spatial filling.
event_mosaic.quantity: Relative LOS change; viewing directions and time windows differ between groups.
event_mosaic.reference: All groups use the same 979 coherent physical reference cells inside the supplied reference. No event pixels are fitted to remove differences. Stability still requires independent justification.

event_measurement.geometry: Multiple same-direction tracks/frames; different LOS vectors are retained, not decomposed into east/up.

event_selection.selection: shortest strictly bracketing pair within each group

support.mode: Union event mosaic; fixed common support only within each acquisition group, not across groups.

independent_validation.status: not evaluated: mosaics have different spatial support and geometry; validate each group separately

warnings: Event mosaics can combine different LOS directions, dates and reference origins. Read each source group before comparing colours across seams.
Free disk space is checked again before array and export writes. Other applications can consume space after this check.

report.headline: What these observations show
findings: 3 event groups (shared physical cells) map 22517.263 km² of the selected region.
Relative LOS displacement median -2.245 cm; p10 -19.176, p90 7.877 cm across mapped cells. These describe this mosaic’s spatial values, not earthquake-only motion or uncertainty.
Inspect per-group dates, references and the source key before comparing this multi-view display with a published map.

Overlapping referenced LOS views differ by a spatial median 0.487 cm and p90 4.620 cm. These are differences between views, not accuracy bounds. Check this disagreement before interpreting a mosaic seam as ground change.
report.comparison_basis: Union event mosaic; fixed common support only within each acquisition group, not across groups.
next_checks: Inspect each source group and overlap differences.
Compare against georeferenced independent displacement data.
report.validation: Engineering behavior can be tested; independent geophysical accuracy is not established.

reading_guide.measurement: Relative LOS displacement across an event-bracketing interval, or a coverage mosaic of separately measured groups.
reading_guide.colours: Positive cm is toward the satellite and negative away, relative to the reference. Zero is relative zero, not proof of unchanged terrain. A mosaic can mix viewing directions and intervals; it cannot by itself separate east/west from vertical motion.
reading_guide.checks: Check the event time, actual before/after dates, coherence, reference support and independent stability. Inspect individual groups, source-index and overlap-difference maps before interpreting seams. Spatial percentiles and overlap spread are not accuracy bounds.
reading_guide.cannot: The pair contains all movement during its interval; it cannot isolate individual shocks, prove earthquake causation at every pixel or map building damage.
reading_guide.validation: Source checksums verify input integrity. Replay checks verify reproducibility. Neither establishes independent environmental accuracy for this run.
